documents.title: What is Artificial Intelligence?
documents.content: Artificial Intelligence (AI) refers to the simulation of human intelligence in machines that are programmed to think, learn, and solve problems. It encompasses a broad range of technologies and approaches aimed at enabling computers to perform tasks that typically require human cognition. AI is built on the foundation of machine learning, and includes sub-areas such as generative AI, text analysis, speech, computer vision, and information extraction.

documents.title: Responsible AI
documents.content: Responsible AI means developing and deploying AI systems in a way that is ethical, transparent, and accountable. It focuses on designing AI that respects human rights, promotes fairness, and reduces risks such as bias and privacy violations. Microsoft's responsible AI principles cover fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency, and accountability.

documents.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
documents.content: Machine Learning is a subset of AI focused on developing algorithms that enable computers to learn from data and make predictions without being explicitly programmed for every scenario. A model is trained on input values called features, which describe observable characteristics of something being studied, and produces a predicted output called a label. Machine learning broadly divides into supervised learning, where models train on labeled examples, and unsupervised learning, where models discover patterns in data without predefined labels.

documents.title: Regression
documents.content: Regression is a supervised machine learning technique for predicting continuous numerical values from input data. For example, a model might predict a house price from its size, or the number of ice creams sold based on temperature. Linear regression assumes a straight-line relationship between inputs and output, while more complex techniques can capture non-linear patterns.

documents.title: Classification
documents.content: Classification is a supervised machine learning technique for assigning entities to predefined categories called classes. Binary classification predicts one of two possible outcomes, such as whether an email is spam or not, while multiclass classification predicts one of three or more categories, such as identifying the species of a plant from its measurements. Classification models learn patterns from labeled training data and use them to calculate the probability that a new input belongs to each possible class.

documents.title: Clustering
documents.content: Clustering is an unsupervised machine learning technique that groups similar entities together based on shared features, without using labeled data. For example, a retailer might cluster customers by purchasing behavior to identify distinct market segments. Common algorithms include K-means and hierarchical clustering, and the technique is widely used in market research, anomaly detection, and data exploration.

documents.title: Deep Learning and Neural Networks
documents.content: Deep learning is a type of machine learning that uses artificial neural networks with many layers to recognize complex patterns in data. These networks pass information through layers of connected nodes, adjusting connection strengths during training to minimize prediction errors. Deep learning powers capabilities such as image recognition, speech processing, natural language understanding, and large language models.

documents.title: Introduction to Generative AI
documents.content: Generative AI refers to artificial intelligence models that can produce new content such as text, images, audio, or video, based on patterns they learned during training. Most modern generative AI models are large language models built on transformer architectures, which allow them to understand context and generate coherent, relevant responses. Users interact with these models by providing a natural language prompt, and prompt engineering is the practice of designing effective prompts to guide the model toward the desired output.

documents.title: Large Language Models
documents.content: Large Language Models are AI models trained to understand and generate human language at scale. They use transformer architectures that break text into tokens, convert those tokens into high-dimensional vectors called embeddings to capture meaning in context, and apply attention mechanisms to understand how tokens relate to one another. LLMs can perform a wide range of tasks including writing, translation, summarization, and question answering without needing to be retrained for each new task.

documents.title: AI Agents
documents.content: AI agents are generative AI applications that perform tasks or make decisions on behalf of users. An agent combines a large language model as its reasoning engine, instructions defining its purpose and behavior, and tools that connect it to external systems for information or actions. For example, an agent might answer expense policy questions and automatically submit expense claims.

documents.title: Transformer models and Attention
documents.content: Transformer models underpin most modern AI systems, including large language models and computer vision models. They represent input as tokens mapped to embedding vectors, and use self-attention to weigh how much each token influences every other, capturing long-range relationships. Encoder components process the input while decoder components generate output, and multi-head attention lets the model consider multiple types of relationships simultaneously.

documents.title: Prompt Engineering
documents.content: Prompt engineering is the practice of crafting effective natural language inputs to guide generative AI models toward accurate, useful responses. Techniques include writing clear instructions, providing context, and including worked examples so the model understands the expected format. Few-shot prompting provides input-output examples in the prompt, while zero-shot prompting relies on the model's existing knowledge without examples.

documents.title: Fine-tuning and Custom Models
documents.content: Fine-tuning adapts a pre-trained large language model to a specific task by continuing training on a smaller, task-specific dataset. This lets the model specialize using far less data than training from scratch, leveraging the broad knowledge it already has. Fine-tuning is commonly used to tailor models to industry-specific terminology or workflows, producing what is called a custom model.

documents.title: Evaluation of Generative AI Models
documents.content: Evaluating generative AI models ensures their outputs meet the required standards for quality and usefulness. Key dimensions include accuracy, which measures how well outputs match expected results; coherence, which checks whether generated text flows logically; relevance, which assesses how well responses address the input prompt; and diversity, which looks at the variety of outputs across multiple runs. Evaluation can combine automated scoring with human review, and continuous testing helps teams catch regressions and improve model performance over time.

documents.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
documents.content: Retrieval-Augmented Generation combines a generative AI model with external knowledge retrieval to improve accuracy and relevance. At query time, the system retrieves relevant documents or data and includes them in the prompt for the model to reason over. This is especially useful when answers depend on up-to-date or domain-specific information not present in the model's training data.

documents.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
documents.content: The Model Context Protocol is a standardized interface that allows AI agents to discover and connect to external tools and services. Rather than requiring custom code for each integration, agents that support MCP can automatically find and use any compatible tool, such as a database, an API, or a software service. This makes it much easier to build agents that can take real-world actions, and enables tools from different providers to work together seamlessly.

documents.title: Common Text Analysis Techniques
documents.content: Text analysis covers techniques for extracting meaning from text. Term Frequency measures how often a word appears in a document, while TF-IDF also considers how rare the word is across a collection to highlight the most distinctive terms. Stemming and lemmatization reduce words to their root form, and parts-of-speech tagging labels each word as a noun, verb, adjective, and so on.

documents.title: Natural Language Processing
documents.content: Natural Language Processing (NLP) is a field of artificial intelligence that focuses on the interaction between computers and human language. It involves the development of algorithms and models that enable machines to understand, interpret, and generate human language in a meaningful way; including generative AI large language models. NLP techniques are used in various text analysis applications such as keyword extraction, sentiment analysis, and summarization.

documents.title: Text Summarization
documents.content: Text summarization automatically generates a concise and coherent summary of a longer document while preserving its key information. Extractive summarization selects and combines the most important sentences from the original text without modifying them, with algorithms like TextRank using graph-based scoring to rank sentences by importance. Abstractive summarization, typically powered by large language models, generates new sentences that rephrase and condense the content, similar to how a human writer would paraphrase a document.

documents.title: Key Term Extraction
documents.content: Key term extraction automatically identifies the most important words and phrases in a text document. Extracted terms surface the main topics and themes, and can be used for document indexing, search optimization, and content categorization. Common approaches combine statistical methods like TF-IDF with linguistic features such as noun phrase detection.

documents.title: Text Classification
documents.content: Text classification assigns predefined labels to text documents based on their content using supervised machine learning. Common applications include spam detection, topic categorization, and language identification. Sentiment analysis is a specialized form that determines whether text expresses a positive, negative, or neutral opinion, widely used in social media monitoring and customer feedback analysis.

documents.title: Overview of Speech
documents.content: Speech technologies enable computers to understand and generate human speech. Common use cases include voice assistants, transcription services that convert spoken words to text, accessibility tools for people with disabilities, language translation, and automated customer service systems. Speech processing involves two main tasks: Speech Recognition (converting spoken words to text) and Speech Synthesis (converting text to spoken words). These technologies have become increasingly accurate and natural-sounding with advances in deep learning and neural networks.

documents.title: Speech Recognition (Speech to Text)
documents.content: Speech recognition converts spoken language into written text by analyzing audio in stages. An acoustic model identifies phonemes from the audio signal, and a language model uses those phonemes with linguistic context to predict the most likely word sequence. Modern systems use deep learning to achieve high accuracy across different speakers, accents, and recording conditions.

documents.title: Speech Synthesis (Text to Speech)
documents.content: Speech synthesis, also called text-to-speech, converts written text into spoken audio. The system maps written characters to their corresponding speech sounds, then applies prosody rules to determine the rhythm, pitch, and emphasis that make speech sound natural and expressive. A neural vocoder then generates the final audio waveform from those parameters. Modern text-to-speech systems use deep learning to produce highly natural voices that closely resemble human speech.

documents.title: Computer Vision Overview
documents.content: Computer vision enables computers to understand and interpret visual information from images and videos. Common tasks include image classification to identify scene contents, object detection to locate and label individual objects, and semantic segmentation to classify every pixel. Convolutional neural networks and vision transformers are the main model types, applied in autonomous vehicles, medical imaging, facial recognition, and augmented reality.

documents.title: Image Processing
documents.content: Image processing involves analyzing and manipulating digital images to extract information or improve quality. Images are made up of pixels, and filters are mathematical operations applied to detect features or reduce noise — for example, edge detection highlights boundaries and blur filters smooth an image. Convolution is the core operation, sliding a small matrix called a kernel across the image to produce a transformed output.

documents.title: Convolutional Neural Networks
documents.content: Convolutional Neural Networks are deep learning models designed for image processing. Convolutional layers apply learned filters to detect edges and textures in early layers and complex shapes in deeper layers, while pooling layers reduce spatial dimensions to lower compute cost. Fully connected layers at the end combine the extracted features to make final predictions, such as assigning an image to a category.

documents.title: Vision Transformers
documents.content: Vision Transformers apply the transformer architecture to image data by dividing an image into fixed-size patches, converting each patch to an embedding vector, and processing them with self-attention to capture relationships across the image. Multimodal models extend this by representing images and text in a shared embedding space, enabling tasks like image captioning, visual question answering, and image-text matching.

documents.title: Image Generation
documents.content: Image generation uses AI to create new images from scratch, typically guided by a text prompt. Diffusion models learn to reverse a gradual noise-adding process, generating images by progressively refining random noise until a coherent picture emerges. This technique powers systems like DALL-E and Stable Diffusion, and has been extended to video generation as well.

documents.title: Overview of Information Extraction
documents.content: Information extraction automatically pulls structured data from unstructured documents such as invoices, receipts, and contracts. The typical workflow starts with optical character recognition to read text from scanned pages, followed by field extraction to identify data points like dates, amounts, and names, then normalization into a consistent format. This technology automates document-heavy workflows in finance, healthcare, and legal services.

documents.title: Optical Character Recognition (OCR)
documents.content: Optical character recognition converts images of text into machine-readable digital text. The process first detects and locates regions of an image that contain text, then recognizes the individual characters within those regions and transcribes them. Modern OCR systems use deep learning to handle challenging inputs such as handwritten text, low-quality scans, skewed pages, and complex layouts with tables or mixed fonts. OCR is a foundational technology for digitizing printed documents and enabling automated document processing.

documents.title: Field Extraction and Mapping
documents.content: Field extraction identifies specific pieces of information in text, such as dates, amounts, names, and addresses, using techniques like named entity recognition, pattern matching, and machine learning. Field mapping then associates those extracted values with the corresponding fields in a target database or application schema. A normalization step converts the values into consistent formats, for example transforming various date representations into a single standard form, so the data can be reliably used in downstream systems.

documents.title: Microsoft Foundry
documents.content: Microsoft Foundry is a comprehensive platform designed to accelerate the development, deployment, and management of AI apps and agents on Microsoft Azure. It provides tools and services that you can use to deploy and manage models, develop agents, and evaluate AI solutions.

documents.title: Foundry Tools
documents.content: Microsoft Foundry includes tools that enable developers to build and deploy AI applications on Azure. These tools include Azure Language for natural language processing tasks, Azure Speech for speech recognition and synthesis, Azure Translator for language translation, and Azure Content Understanding for extracting insights from unstructured data.

documents.title: Foundry Models
documents.content: Foundry Models is a model catalog that includes models from Microsoft, OpenAI, and other model providers.

documents.title: Foundry Agent Development
documents.content: Microsoft Foundry enables developers to create AI agents that can perform tasks autonomously. The Foundry agent service provides tools and APIs for defining agent behavior, integrating with external systems, and managing agent interactions.

documents.title: Foundry SDKs and APIs
documents.content: Developers can use SDKs and APIs to build AI apps and agents with Microsoft Foundry. The Foundry SDK enables programmatic access to projects, agents, and other Foundry resources, while the OpenAI API enables developers to integrate powerful language models into their applications. Within the OpenAI API, the Responses API and ChatCompletions APIs provide interfaces for generating responses and managing conversations with large language models.

documents.title: Foundry Toolkit for Visual Studio Code
documents.content: Visual Studio Code is a popular code editor that supports a wide range of extensions and tools for developers. Developers can use the Foundry Toolkit for Visual Studio Code to build AI apps and agents on Microsoft Foundry. The toolkit provides integration with the Foundry SDK, enabling programmatic access to projects, agents, and other Foundry resources.

documents.title: Foundry IQ
documents.content: Foundry IQ is a managed knowledge layer that agents can use to access enterprise data. With Foundry IQ, you create a knowledge base that connects to one or more knowledge sources. Foundry IQ is built on Azure AI Search's agentic retrieval capabilities.

documents.title: Open AI models in Foundry
documents.content: Microsoft Foundry Models include the latest models from OpenAI; including multiple generations of GPT models, which can be used for a wide range of natural language processing tasks such as text generation, summarization, translation, and more.

documents.title: Anthropic models in Foundry
documents.content: Microsoft Foundry Models include models from Anthropic, which provides access to powerful language models like Claude that can be used for various applications such as content generation, code generation, and conversational agents.

documents.title: Authentication in Foundry
documents.content: Microsoft Foundry secures access to its resources through robust authentication mechanisms, including key-based authentication and integration with Microsoft Entra ID. Client applications must authenticate using API keys or managed identity credentials to access models and agents.

documents.title: Microsoft AI Certifications
documents.content: Microsoft certifications provide a way to validate your competency in AI-related roles. AI-related certification exams cover a range of topics, including AI fundamentals, AI app and agent development, AI cloud solution architecture, and machine learning operations.

documents.title: Microsoft AI Credentials
documents.content: Microsoft Applied Skills credentials provide a way to demonstrate your ability to perform specific tasks related to AI. These credentials are designed to be more focused than traditional exam-based certifications, enabling you to showcase your skills in a practical test.
